paper.title: The Role of Transparency in Repeated First-Price Auctions with Unknown Valuations

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic i.i.d. environment, bandit feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Repeated first-price auction: bid b in [0,1], utility (V_t-b)1{b>=M_t}; valuation V_t unknown before bidding
Bandit feedback: V_t observed only when the auction is won, M_t never observed
Utility is neither Lipschitz nor continuous in the bid
(V_t,M_t) pairs i.i.d. from an arbitrary (possibly non-smooth) joint distribution
settings.definition_quote: Stochastic i.i.d.: The pairs $(V_1,M_1),(V_2,M_2),\dots$ are a stochastic i.i.d.\ process. ... The learner observes $V_t$ if it gets the item and the symbol $\star$ otherwise

unmapped: Repeated first-price auction with unknown valuations, bids in [0,1]
Semi-transparent feedback: V_t observed if auction won, M_t observed if lost

settings.definition_quote: Semi-transparent feedback. The learner observes $V_t$ if it gets the item and $M_t$ otherwise: $Z_t$ is equal to $(\star,M_t)$ if $B_t < M_t$ and to $(V_t,\star)$ otherwise.

unmapped: Repeated first-price auction with unknown valuations
Transparent feedback: M_t always observed, V_t observed only when the auction is won (a strongly observable feedback-graph-like structure)

settings.definition_quote: Transparent feedback. The learner always observes $M_t$, but $V_t$ is only revealed if it gets the item: $Z_t$ is equal to $(\star,M_t)$ if $B_t < M_t$ and to $(V_t,M_t)$ otherwise.

algorithms.name: W.T.FPA (Wrapper for Transparent First-Price Auctions) with Exp3.FPA base learners
Discretized Bandit with rescaled Poly INF

source.label: thm:lower-iid-general-bandit
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in a stochastic i.i.d.\ environment with bandit feedback. Then, any learning algorithm $\cA$ satisfies $R_T(\cA) \ge \tfrac 1{13} T $.

results.notes: Regret is sup_b E[...], i.e. pseudo-regret-type. Needle-in-haystack construction.

source.label: thm:upper-iid-general-semi-transparent
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in a stochastic i.i.d.\ environment with semi-transparent feedback. Then there exists a learning algorithm $\cA$ such that $R_T(\cA) \le 16 \brb{ 13 + \sqrt{\ln T} } T^{\nicefrac 23}$.

symbols.sigma_s: smoothness parameter of the distribution of (V_t,M_t)

source.label: thm:lower-iid-smooth-semi-transparent
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in a stochastic i.i.d.\ $\sigma$-smooth environment with semi-transparent feedback, for $\sigma \in (0,\nicefrac 1{66}]$. Then, any learning algorithm $\cA$ satisfies, for $T \ge 8$, $R_T(\cA) \ge \frac{3}{10^4}T^{\nicefrac 23}$.

results.notes: Also implies lower bound for bandit feedback and smooth adversarial settings (weaker feedback / more general env).

tuning: epoch tau base learner Exp3.FPA with gamma = sqrt(ln|X_tau| / ((e-1) 2^{tau-1}))

source.label: thm:upper-iid-general-transparent
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in a stochastic i.i.d.\ environment with transparent feedback. Then there exists a learning algorithm $\cA$ such that \[ R_T(\cA) \le 3 + 2\brb{ \sqrt{2}+2 }\brb{ \sqrt{2(e-1)} + 8 } \sqrt{T \ln T} \;. \]

results.notes: Wrapper uses geometric epochs without T, so anytime (inferred). Derived from Proposition 1 (generic wrapper bound, not recorded separately) and Proposition 2.

source.label: thm:lower-iid-smooth-full
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in a stochastic i.i.d.\ $\sigma$-smooth environment with full feedback, for $\sigma \in (0,\nicefrac 19]$. Then, any learning algorithm $\cA$ satisfies $R_T(\cA) \ge \frac1{2048} \sqrt{T}$.

tuning: base learner: Poly INF rescaled to [-1,1]

source.label: thm:upper-adv-smooth-bandit
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in an adversarial $\sigma$-smooth environment with bandit feedback. Then there exists a learning algorithm $\cA$ such that $R_T(\cA) \le \tfrac{29}{\sigma} T^{\nicefrac 23}$.

results.notes: Also applies to smooth i.i.d. and to semi-transparent feedback.

tuning: Exp3.FPA on uniform grid of ceil(sqrt(T))+1 bids

source.label: thm:upper-adv-smooth-transparent
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in an adversarial $\sigma$-smooth environment with transparent feedback. Then there exists a learning algorithm $\cA$ such that $R_T(\cA) \le 6\left(\frac{1}{\sigma} + \sqrt{\ln T}\right) \sqrt{T}$.

source.label: thm:lower-adv-general-full
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bidding in first-price auctions in an adversarial environment with full feedback. Then, any learning algorithm $\cA$ satisfies $R_T(\cA) \ge \nicefrac{T}{24} $.

results.notes: Hard instance is a randomized sequence (Yao's principle).

source.label: prop:routine
source.quote: Let $ \cX \subset [0,1]$ be a finite set, $T\in \N$ a time horizon, and tune the exploration rate as $\gamma = \sqrt{\fracc { \ln ( \labs{\cX} ) }{ (e-1)T }}$. Then, the regret of \expthreefpa{} against the best fixed bid in $\cX$ is ... $\le 2 \sqrt{(e-1) \ln \brb{ \labs{\cX} } T }$

results.notes: Environment type not explicit; proof holds for any sequence of (V_t,M_t) independent of the learner's randomness, recorded as oblivious adversarial.
